segment.description: Big Soddy Creek (locally 'Soddy Creek'), Hamilton County, draining the Soddy Creek Gorge country on Walden Ridge into Chickamauga Lake at Soddy-Daisy (Tennessee River HUC 06020001). TWRA stocks rainbow trout with a Seasonal (spring) program plus a Delayed-Harvest reach; the DH regulations define the special-regulation water as 'Big Soddy Creek: Upstream of Back Valley Road.'
segment.boundaries: TWRA Delayed-Harvest reach: upstream of Back Valley Road (C&R season Nov 1 - Feb 28). USGS temperature record is at the lower creek (03566400 'SODDY CREEK AT SODDY' near the US-27 corridor/lake arm) and speaks to the lower reach, not the gorge DH reach.

coldSource.notes: Creek drains the Soddy Creek Gorge / Cumberland Trail section on the Walden Ridge escarpment above Soddy-Daisy, but no agency-published elevation or gorge microclimate figure was located. No creek-specific mining/AMD water-quality report was found: the closest peer-reviewed coal-drainage literature covers neighboring North Chickamauga Creek (OSTI 20727845, pH 3.6 fishless AMD zone), not Big Soddy - no impact is inferred here.

holdover.detail: No holdover study or creel evidence found. The Delayed-Harvest design (stockings in late Oct and Nov, catch-and-release Nov 1 - Feb 28 upstream of Back Valley Road, harvest reopening March) keeps stocked rainbows in the creek through winter by program design, but no agency documentation of trout carrying over into the following summer exists.

wildPopulation.detail: Not on TWRA's Wild Trout Streams list - the creek's only trout regulation entry is the Delayed-Harvest reach (upstream of Back Valley Road); no wild trout survey or self-sustaining population documentation found.

segment.description: Citico Creek main stem, Monroe County, in the Cherokee National Forest, flowing north to Tellico Lake (Little Tennessee HUC 06010204). The catalog covers both the stocked main stem and the wild-trout headwater forks. TWRA's Tellico-Citico Permit Area regulates the creek from its confluence with Little Citico Creek upstream to the confluence of the North and South Forks; the North/South Fork headwaters (incl. Falls Branch, a South Fork tributary) hold the documented wild brook trout.
segment.boundaries: Permitted reach: Little Citico Creek confluence upstream to the North/South Fork junction (TWRA trout regulations page). Stocked reach is the main stem; wild trout are documented in the forks above.

coldSource.notes: Elevation figure applies to the headwaters, not the main stem: the TWRA Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 places Goat Falls on North Fork Citico Creek 'at ~3,200' (brook trout habitat discussion) - https://www.tn.gov/content/dam/tn/twra/documents/fishing/Tennessee-Trout-Management-Plan-2017-2027.pdf . The plan also describes the watershed as steep, remote, rain-flashy Cherokee NF terrain. No dam on the creek; cold source is forested mountain headwater elevation.

holdover.detail: No site-specific holdover study found. The main stem receives 22 consecutive weekly TWRA seasonal stockings (weeks of 2/22 through 7/19 in the 2026 schedule) and the permit area remains open to daily fishing Aug 16 - end of February without a permit, which implies fish availability into fall/winter, but no creel or tag-return evidence of holdover was located.

wildPopulation.detail: TWRA's Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 documents that until recently two streams in the Citico Creek watershed supported brook trout - upper North Fork Citico Creek and Falls Branch (South Fork Citico tributary); a 2013 distribution survey found only the Falls Branch population remains (naturalized, hatchery origin per 1990s genetics), with North Fork Citico extirpated above Goat Falls. USFS Cherokee NF states 'Wild trout, rainbow, brown and native brookies are present in most of the mountain streams above 1000 feet' (general CNF statement, not Citico-specific). The stocked main stem itself is not a wild trout water and is NOT on TWRA's Wild Trout Streams list.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: A naturalized brook trout population persisted in the watershed (Falls Branch, 2013 TWRA survey) - documented year-round survival in the headwaters - while the stocked main stem showed ~23 C grab temperatures in June 2014 near its mouth, consistent with its put-grow-take role rather than fail.

segment.description: Conasauga River (GNIS 00327507), Coosa-basin drainage — restricted to the TENNESSEE reaches the catalog entry covers. TDEC designates the Tennessee reach as a State Scenic River: 'The entire segment of the river in Polk County, upstream from the Highway 411 bridge', Class I Natural River Area, designated April 23, 1969, ~10.1 miles, one of only two Tennessee Scenic Rivers in the Cherokee National Forest. The river crosses the TN/GA line more than once near Tennga; the famous rare-species research (Conasauga logperch, amber darter, listed mussels) and Georgia's 2015 Outstanding National Resource Water designation apply to the GEORGIA reaches (Cohutta Wilderness headwaters, Jacks River) and are NOT attributed to the Tennessee reach here.
segment.boundaries: Polk County segments of the river upstream of the US-411 bridge (take-out 35.00888, -84.73389, at the state line near Tennga) per the TDEC Scenic Rivers designation; the USGS gauge 02384000 'CONASAUGA RIVER AT US 411, NEAR TENNGA' (35.0095, -84.7338, 108 sq mi — listed under Polk County TN, operated by the USGS Georgia center) sits at the downstream boundary of this reach.

coldSource.notes: Freestone river draining the Cohutta Mountains through the Cherokee National Forest; the Tennessee scenic segment is a narrow valley run with Class II-III rapids per TDEC's paddling description. No dam, no spring-influence documentation for the TN reach. Gauge altitude at the US-411 boundary is ~756 ft (USGS 02384000), so the TN reach is low-elevation; no agency statement on TN-reach summer cold-water refuge was located.

holdover.detail: No trout presence of any kind documented for the Tennessee reach — no stocking program rows, no trout designation, no creel or angler documentation located — so holdover cannot be assessed.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documented in the Tennessee reach. TDEC's Scenic River page describes a rich native fish community — 'more than 90 fish species and 25 mussel species' with federal and state-listed aquatic species — and names no trout. The celebrated rare-fish work and any trout headwater fishery (Cohutta Wilderness, Jacks River, GA's 2015 ONRW designation) are on the Georgia reaches and do not transfer to the TN reach. TWRA's stocking workbook contains zero Conasauga rows, and the river is absent from TWRA's wild-trout/special-regulation lists.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: The only summer data for the Tennessee reach — USGS grabs at the US-411 state-line crossing bounding it — read 20.0-24.0 degC (1957-1996), marginal for trout, and no source documents any trout presence, stocking, or fishery on the TN reach itself.

segment.description: Nickajack Lake / Nickajack Reservoir — the TVA mainstem Tennessee River impoundment formed by Nickajack Dam (at Tennessee River mile 427.7, near New Hope in Marion County, impounded 1967) and backing 46 miles upstream through Chattanooga to Chickamauga Dam (catalog: Marion/Hamilton counties). TWRA documents the fishery entirely as warmwater: largemouth/smallmouth/spotted bass, crappie, bluegill/redear, catfish, white/striped/hybrid bass, sauger, walleye, paddlefish — 'no mention of trout or trout stocking anywhere on this page'. At full summer pool it covers 10,370 acres with 192 miles of shoreline (TWRA). The USGS tailwater gauge at the dam is 03570525 'TENNESSEE RIVER AT NICKAJACK DAM (TAILWATER), TN'.
segment.boundaries: Nickajack Dam upstream to Chickamauga Dam, Tennessee portion (the downstream continuation toward Guntersville Lake in Alabama is cataloged separately as tennessee-river).

coldSource.notes: Mainstem run-of-river reservoir: TVA operates Nickajack near a constant full pool (~633.5-634 ft) with a short retention time of roughly 3-4 days, so the impoundment tracks mainstem Tennessee River temperature rather than behaving like a cold deep-release storage project; no selective cold-water withdrawal regime is documented for the dam. The tailwater gauge record (below) shows warm releases. elevationFt = full pool per TVA data (~633.5-634 ft; TVA land-plan summary ~10,200 acres vs TWRA's 10,370).

holdover.detail: No trout fishery of any kind is documented: zero Nickajack rows in TWRA's 2026 trout stocking workbook, the reservoir is absent from the TWRA Trout Management Plan's list of the nine Tennessee reservoirs that support trout fisheries (Dale Hollow, Parksville, South Holston, Wilbur, Watauga, Fort Patrick Henry, Calderwood, Chilhowee, Tellico), and TWRA's Nickajack Reservoir page lists no trout and no holdover fishery.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documented. TWRA's species list for the reservoir is entirely warmwater (bass, crappie, sunfish, catfish, striped/hybrid bass, sauger/walleye, paddlefish), and the Trout Management Plan's wild-trout discussion limits wild trout to East Tennessee mountain streams with no mention of Nickajack.

coldSource.notes: The catalog names Waterville (upstream generation driving the Hartford whitewater reach) but no agency page retrieved this session verifies the dam's operator or release draw (duke-energy and TDEC Pigeon River URLs 404'd; tva.com blocked in prior passes — the Pigeon is not a TVA reservoir). What TDEC's 2026 303(d) list DOES document is thermal: Cocke County assessment unit TN06010106001_4000 (5.03 mi) is impaired for TEMPERATURE (Low) with source 'DAM OR IMPOUNDMENT', plus FLOW REGIME MODIFICATION (dam), and COLOR from 'INDUSTRIAL POINT SOURCE DISCHARGE' and 'SOURCES OUTSIDE STATE JURISDICTION OR BORDERS' (the Canton NC paper mill signature) — the 303(d) extract prints unit IDs and miles but not boundary text; unit _4000 is the only dam-sourced Pigeon segment and the 5.03-mile length matches the Waterville-to-Hartford gorge, so the temperature impairment is attributable to the dam-regulated upper reach. This is a documented WARM-release (temperature non-support) signal, not evidence of cold tailwater. USGS station altitude at Newport is 1,038 ft; the gorge reach upstream is higher but no verified elevation figure was located.

holdover.detail: No holdover documentation exists for the Tennessee reach. The catalog's 'holds trout in cooler months' is an angling-level claim with no agency source found (the USFS Pigeon River area page mentions fishing and whitewater but names no trout for the river).

wildPopulation.detail: No agency record of a trout population on the Tennessee Pigeon was located: the river is absent from TWRA's stocking schedule and wild trout list, and the USFS Cherokee NF Pigeon River area page describes whitewater and fishing without naming trout. (North Carolina's upper-reach trout management is a different jurisdiction and was not transferred to this reach.)

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: TDEC's 2026 303(d) list records a 5.03-mile dam-sourced Cocke County Pigeon River segment as TEMPERATURE-impaired (source 'DAM OR IMPOUNDMENT'), TWRA stocks nothing into the TN reach and manages it under smallmouth (20-in minimum)/walleye quality rules, and the only gauge on the river (Newport, lower reach) recorded 25.7 C in August — no agency evidence of a year-round coldwater reach.
